metadata.title: EAU Guidelines on Sexual and Reproductive Health
metadata.summary: The available sections address the assessment and management of low sexual desire in men, congenital penile curvature and Peyronie’s disease. They cover psychological and endocrine considerations, conservative therapies, surgical selection, treatment risks and graded recommendations. An algorithm outlines treatment decisions for Peyronie’s disease.

target_population: Couples distressed by sexual desire discrepancies

conditions.name: low sexual desire
conditions.description: Reduced sexual desire may arise from interacting biological, psychological and relationship factors. Under ICD-10, loss or absence of desire must be the primary sexual problem rather than a consequence of another accompanying sexual difficulty. Male HSDD describes a persistent or recurrent lack of sexual or erotic thoughts, fantasies and desire for sexual activity; assessment takes age and the individual's broader circumstances into account.
conditions.epidemiology: The exact prevalence is unknown. A population-based survey of middle-aged German men (n = 12,646) reported a prevalence of 4.7%. LSD is less common in men than in women, but is the most frequent presenting complaint in couples' therapy.
conditions.clinical_presentation: Men may report reduced interest in sexual activity with a partner, alone, or both. Negative thoughts or shame during intercourse, anxiety about erections, depression and relationship difficulties may accompany reduced desire. Potential associated conditions include androgen deficiency, hyperprolactinaemia, erectile dysfunction and other illnesses listed as causes in the guideline.

subtypes.name: male hypoactive sexual desire disorder (HSDD)
subtypes.distinguishing_features: Persistent or recurrent deficiency or absence of sexual or erotic thoughts or fantasies and desire for sexual activity.

subtypes.name: dyadic desire
subtypes.distinguishing_features: Desire for sexual activity and intimacy with another person.

subtypes.name: solitary desire
subtypes.distinguishing_features: Interest in sexual activity undertaken alone, potentially without intimacy or sharing with another person.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Characterise the desire concern, classify LSD and identify possible underlying causes, including chronic therapies that may adversely affect desire.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: Initial assessment of a man reporting LSD.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: The history should distinguish a primary desire problem from other accompanying sexual difficulties.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Assess the strength, frequency and personal significance of dyadic and solitary sexual desire through 14 self-administered questions.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: When a validated questionnaire is included in diagnostic assessment.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: Its two desire categories are dyadic and solitary.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Assess depressive symptoms, partner conflict, psychosexual development, expectations about sexuality and performance, dysfunctional thoughts, anxiety triggers and discrepancies in desire between partners.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: Assessment of a man reporting LSD.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: Findings may inform whether referral for psychological intervention or sexual psychotherapy is appropriate.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Identify anatomical abnormalities potentially associated with LSD or another sexual dysfunction, particularly erectile dysfunction.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: Initial assessment of LSD.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Investigate a possible endocrine contribution to reduced desire.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: When accompanying symptoms suggest an endocrinological problem.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Investigate a possible endocrine contribution, including hyperprolactinaemia.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: When accompanying symptoms suggest an endocrinological problem.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Investigate a possible endocrine contribution to reduced desire.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: When accompanying symptoms suggest an endocrinological problem.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Diagnose a prolactin-secreting pituitary adenoma as a possible cause of hyperprolactinaemia-associated LSD.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: In evaluation of a suspected prolactin-secreting pituitary adenoma.

conditions.name: Congenital penile curvature
conditions.description: CPC results from unequal development of the corporal tunica albuginea and is not accompanied by urethral malformation. Curvature is usually ventral, can be lateral and is less often dorsal.
conditions.epidemiology: Reported incidence is < 1%, although studies in the absence of hypospadias have reported prevalence rates of 4-10%.
conditions.clinical_presentation: Presentation usually occurs after puberty, when erections and sexual activity make the curvature more noticeable. More pronounced curvature can hinder or prevent intercourse.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Establish the diagnosis and assess the effects of curvature on sexual activity.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: Suspected CPC.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: History is usually sufficient to establish the diagnosis.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Document curvature and exclude other pathologies.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: Suspected CPC.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Document the curvature and help exclude other pathologies.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: Suspected CPC; an erection induced by intracavernous injection (ICI) of vasoactive drugs is preferred.

conditions.name: Peyronie’s disease
conditions.description: PD involves penile deformity associated with a plaque or nodule. Distinguishing active from stable disease affects medical treatment decisions and the timing of surgery.
conditions.epidemiology: Reported prevalence ranges from 0.4-20.3% and is higher among patients with ED and diabetes. A USA survey reported 0.7% for definitive cases and 11% for probable cases. Typical onset is at 50-60 years, although PD also occurs in men < 40 years, with reported prevalence of 1.5-16.9% in that age group. ED occurs in 30-70.6% of patients with PD.
conditions.clinical_presentation: Possible findings include pain with erection, palpable penile nodules or plaques, curvature or other deformity, changes in penile length or girth, difficulty with penetration, erectile dysfunction and distress related to symptoms. Pain or recent progression of deformity may indicate active disease.

subtypes.name: active disease
subtypes.distinguishing_features: A shorter symptom duration, pain during erection or a recent change in deformity suggests ongoing activity; the treatment algorithm describes pain, worsening deformity and progressive curvature.

subtypes.name: stable disease
subtypes.distinguishing_features: Erection-related pain has resolved and curvature has remained stable for at least three months; the treatment algorithm describes no pain or worsening deformity.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Document symptom duration, erection-related pain, penile deformity, difficulty with vaginal or anal intromission, erectile function, symptom-related distress and potential risk factors for PD and ED.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: Initial evaluation of PD.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: Shorter symptom duration, pain with erection or recent deformity change suggests active disease. Resolution of pain and curvature stability for at least three months support stabilisation.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Measure psychological and physical symptoms, penile pain and symptom bother.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: Especially in clinical trials; routine administration in daily practice is not mandatory.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Assess penile nodules or plaques and examine the hands and feet for related conditions, including Dupuytren’s contracture and Ledderhosen scarring of the plantar fascia.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: Diagnostic evaluation of PD.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: Plaque size does not correlate with the degree of curvature.

diagnostic_workup.test: Stretched or erect penile length measurement
diagnostic_workup.purpose: Inform treatment selection and document length relevant to potential medico-legal considerations.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: Diagnostic evaluation and assessment before reconstructive surgery.

diagnostic_workup.test: Objective assessment of curvature during erection
diagnostic_workup.purpose: Document the degree of curvature and any complex deformity.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: Mandatory in diagnostic assessment; options include home self-photography of a natural erection, preferably, a vacuum-assisted erection test or intracavernous injection (ICI) of vasoactive agents.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: The guideline suggests that ICI provides a superior objective assessment because the induced erection can resemble or exceed an erection during sexual arousal.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Assess erectile function.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: When erectile function is evaluated in PD.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: IIEF has not been validated in patients with PD.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Help identify a plaque and assess its location and calcification.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: When plaque characteristics require assessment, especially before surgery; routine use to measure plaque size or deformity is discouraged.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: Ultrasound measurement of plaque size is inaccurate and operator dependent.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Assess penile haemodynamics and vascular anatomy, investigate ED aetiology, and locate plaques or identify calcification. Assessment of arterial inflow before an intervention such as plaque incision and grafting can help exclude arteriogenic ED.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: Diagnostic evaluation of ED and particularly before surgery.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Assessment of penile curvature or deformity.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: Not recommended for routine diagnostic assessment.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Assessment of penile curvature or deformity.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: Not recommended for routine diagnostic assessment.

diagnostic_workup.test: Pre-operative assessment of plaques, deformity and erectile function
diagnostic_workup.purpose: Document plaque size and location, curvature severity, hinge or hourglass deformity, penile length, erectile function including response to pharmacotherapy when ED is present, and patient expectations.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: Before considering reconstructive surgery.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: These findings inform the choice of surgical approach.

definitions.description: Ongoing pain, worsening penile deformity or progressive curvature; a shorter symptom duration, erection-related pain or recent deformity change also suggests continuing activity.
Pain has resolved and curvature has remained unchanged for at least three months, without deterioration of deformity.

staging.additional_rules: For surgery, the guideline describes stable disease for 3-6 months (or more than 9-12 months after onset of PD); its surgical recommendation requires stability for at least three months and notes that this is usually reached after twelve months from symptom onset.

follow_up.schedule: Periodically reassess pain while monitoring the effect of NSAIDs used for active-phase penile pain.
recommended_tests: Measure and document penile length before and after a tunical shortening procedure.

toxicities.event: Penile haematoma
toxicities.incidence: Among patients treated with CCH, penile haematoma occurred in 50.2%; serious treatment-emergent adverse events, comprising penile haematoma and corporeal rupture, occurred in 0.9%.

management.actions: Local adverse events generally resolved without intervention within 14 days of injection.

prevention: Advise against sexual intercourse for the four weeks after CCH injection to reduce serious treatment-emergent adverse events.

toxicities.event: Penile pain
toxicities.incidence: Penile pain occurred in 33.5% of patients treated with CCH.

management.actions: The local event generally subsided without intervention within 14 days of injection.

toxicities.event: Penile swelling
toxicities.incidence: Penile swelling occurred in 28.9% of patients treated with CCH.

management.actions: The local event generally subsided without intervention within 14 days of injection.

toxicities.event: Injection site pain
toxicities.incidence: Injection site pain occurred in 24.1% of patients treated with CCH.

management.actions: The local event generally subsided without intervention within 14 days of injection.

toxicities.event: Corporeal rupture
toxicities.incidence: Serious treatment-emergent adverse events, comprising penile haematoma and corporeal rupture, occurred in 0.9%; the studies described three corporeal ruptures that underwent surgical repair.

management.actions: Treat surgically; the three reported ruptures were repaired by surgery.

prevention: Advise against sexual intercourse for the four weeks following CCH injection.

toxicities.event: Sinusitis and flu-like symptoms
prevention: NSAIDs given before IFN-α2b injection can effectively address these mild effects.

toxicities.event: Tissue atrophy, skin thinning and immunosuppression
prevention: Do not offer intralesional steroids to reduce penile curvature, plaque size or pain.

toxicities.event: Adverse effects of oral tamoxifen
prevention: Do not offer oral tamoxifen for Peyronie’s disease; the evidence summary cites adverse effects as the reason it is no longer recommended.

toxicities.event: Impaired sexual functioning
prevention: When treating major depression, choose antidepressant compounds with less impact on sexual function.

toxicities.event: Discomfort and inconvenience with penile traction therapy
recognition: Difficulty accommodating device use for 2-8 hours daily

toxicities.event: Penile shortening after tunical shortening procedures
toxicities.incidence: The narrative reports shortening of 1-1.5 cm in 22-69% of patients. In Table 8.2, significant shortening is reported for Nesbit: 8.7% (5-39); Modified Nesbit: 3.2% (0-13); Yachia: 3.5% (0-10); 16-dot / mod16-dot: 5.9% (0-6); and Simple plication: 8.9% (0-55). Any shortening is reported for Nesbit: 21.8% (9-39); Modified Nesbit: 58.% (23-74); Yachia: 69% (47-97); 16-dot / mod16-dot: 44.6% (40-52); and Simple plication: 33.4% (0-90). Table values are weighted averages, with ranges in parentheses.
recognition: Perceived loss of length may exceed measured shortening
prevention: Measure and record penile length before and after straightening, regardless of the surgical technique.
Discuss the possibility of shortening before surgery.

toxicities.event: Penile shortening after tunical lengthening procedures
toxicities.incidence: Table 8.3 reports postoperative shortening for autologous grafts: Dermis, 59.9% (40-75); Vein grafts, 32.7% (0-100); Tunica albuginea, 16.3% (13-18); Tunica vaginalis, 32.2% (0-83); Temporalis fascia / Fascia lata, 0%; Buccal mucosa, 15.2% (0-80). For cadaveric allografts: Pericardium, 23.1% (0-33); Fascia lata, 28.6%; Dura matter, 30%. For xenografts: Porcine SIS, 19.6% (0-66); Bovine pericardium, 20.1% (0-79.4); Bovine dermis, 0%; Porcine dermis, 78.9%; TachoSil®, 13.4% (0-93). Table values are weighted averages, with ranges in parentheses.
recognition: Loss of penile length after grafting
prevention: Postoperative VED and PTT have been proposed to prevent penile length loss of up to 1.5 cm.
Discuss shortening as a surgical risk before treatment.

toxicities.event: Postoperative de novo ED after tunical shortening procedures
toxicities.incidence: Table 8.2 reports postoperative de novo ED for Nesbit: 6.9% (0-17); Modified Nesbit: 3% (0-13); Yachia: 9.6% (0-13); 16-dot / mod16-dot: 3.8% (0-13); and Simple plication: 8.1% (0-38). These are weighted averages, with ranges in parentheses.
prevention: Discuss the risk of ED before surgery.

toxicities.event: Postoperative de novo ED after tunical lengthening procedures
toxicities.incidence: The narrative describes a postoperative ED risk of up to 50% for patients without preoperative ED. Table 8.3 reports de novo ED for autologous grafts: Dermis, 20.5% (7-67); Vein grafts, 14.8% (0-37); Tunica albuginea, 17.8% (0-24); Tunica vaginalis, 9.6% (0-41); Temporalis fascia / Fascia lata, 0%; Buccal mucosa, 5.3% (0-10). For cadaveric allografts: Pericardium, 37.8% (30-63); Fascia lata, 7.1%; Dura matter, 17.4% (15-23). For xenografts: Porcine SIS, 21.9% (7-54); Bovine pericardium, 26.5% (0-50); Bovine dermis, 25%; Porcine dermis, 63%; TachoSil®, 13% (0-21). Table values are weighted averages, with ranges in parentheses.
prevention: Inform patients without preoperative ED of the postoperative risk.
Daily nocturnal PDE5I may improve graft perfusion and minimise postoperative ED rates.

toxicities.event: Penile hypoesthesia or numbness after surgery
associated_therapies: Tunical lengthening procedures involving dorsal neurovascular bundle mobilisation
toxicities.incidence: Table 8.2 reports penile hypoesthesia for Nesbit: 11. 8% (2-60); Modified Nesbit: 5.6% (0-31); Yachia: 1% (0-3); 16-dot / mod16-dot: 8.2% (6-13); and Simple plication: 9% (0-47). These are weighted averages, with ranges in parentheses. The narrative describes recurrent curvature and hypoesthesia after tunical shortening as uncommon (~10%).
recognition: Numbness following mobilisation of the dorsal neurovascular bundle
prevention: Discuss numbness before surgery.

toxicities.event: Recurrent or residual penile curvature after surgery
toxicities.incidence: The narrative describes recurrence after tunical shortening as uncommon (~10%).
recognition: Persistence or return of penile curvature
prevention: Wait for disease stabilisation before surgery.
Use non-absorbable or slowly re-absorbed sutures rather than sutures that lose tensile strength before the repair gains adequate strength.
Explain the risks of recurrence and residual curvature before surgery.

toxicities.event: Penile skin irritation from suture knots
recognition: Irritation where knots are palpable beneath penile skin
prevention: Bury non-absorbable suture knots; slowly re-absorbable sutures may lessen this problem.

toxicities.event: Graft-related infection, inflammation, fibrosis, contracture or allergic reactions
recognition: Secondary graft inflammation with tissue fibrosis
prevention: Avoid synthetic grafts in Peyronie’s disease reconstructive surgery.

toxicities.event: Infection concern with cadaveric dura mater
prevention: Cadaveric dura mater is no longer used because of concern about possible infection.

toxicities.event: Postoperative phimosis
prevention: Consider circumcision with penile degloving to prevent postoperative phimosis; the document also notes a study suggesting circumcision is not invariably necessary when the foreskin is normal before surgery.

toxicities.event: Glans necrosis
prevention: Do not use the sliding technique because serious, potentially life-changing complications, including glans necrosis, have been reported.

toxicities.event: Urethral perforation during prosthesis modelling
toxicities.incidence: A risk of 3% was reported among patients undergoing modelling over the inflated prosthesis.

toxicities.event: Penile shortening after penile prosthesis implantation
prevention: Counsel patients with Peyronie’s disease that a prosthesis is not intended to restore their former penile length.

prophylaxis.recommendation: Advise patients to avoid sexual intercourse after CCH injection to prevent serious treatment-emergent adverse events.
prophylaxis.target_population: Men receiving CCH for Peyronie’s disease

prophylaxis.recommendation: NSAIDs before IFN-α2b injection can effectively address its mild sinusitis and flu-like effects.
Consider circumcision with penile degloving as a means of preventing postoperative phimosis; one study suggests it may be unnecessary when the foreskin is normal preoperatively.
prophylaxis.target_population: Patients undergoing penile degloving for Peyronie’s disease surgery

prophylaxis.recommendation: Postoperative penile rehabilitation with VED or PTT has been suggested to prevent penile length loss of up to 1.5 cm.
Daily nocturnal PDE5I may enhance graft perfusion and minimise postoperative ED rates.
prophylaxis.target_population: Patients after grafting surgery for Peyronie’s disease

prophylaxis.recommendation: Use non-absorbable or slowly re-absorbed sutures to reduce recurrent curvature associated with premature loss of suture strength.

therapies_index.name: Psychological interventions
approved_indications: May benefit men with low sexual desire when focused on cognitive and behavioural strategies; efficacy data are scarce.

therapies_index.name: Mindfulness treatments
approved_indications: Identified as a possible approach for low sexual desire, although evidence for psychological interventions is limited.

therapies_index.name: Psychotherapy
approved_indications: May improve the effectiveness of pharmacotherapy when low sexual desire is related to depression.

therapies_index.name: testosterone therapy
approved_indications: Low sexual desire accompanied by signs and symptoms of testosterone deficiency.
therapies_index.administration: Different formulations may be used; treatment aims to bring testosterone into the physiological range.
monitoring: Assess whether testosterone reaches the physiological range.

therapies_index.name: dopamine agonist agents
approved_indications: Prolactin-secreting pituitary adenomas associated with hyperprolactinaemia and low sexual desire.

therapies_index.name: antidepressant therapy
approved_indications: Major depression associated with low sexual desire; compounds with less effect on sexual function should be selected.
key_toxicities: Antidepressants may adversely affect sexual functioning.

therapies_index.name: surgery
approved_indications: Definitive treatment for congenital penile curvature; surgery may be undertaken after puberty when intercourse is significantly impaired.
Peyronie’s disease with stable deformity that compromises intercourse.
therapies_index.administration: The choice of operation depends on deformity, penile length, erectile function and patient preference.
key_toxicities: Potential penile shortening, erectile dysfunction, numbness, delayed orgasm, recurrent or residual curvature and palpable sutures.

therapies_index.name: Nesbit procedure
therapies_index.mechanism: An elliptical portion of tunica albuginea is excised opposite the point of greatest curvature to shorten the convex side.
approved_indications: Correction of congenital penile curvature.
Tunical shortening for selected patients with Peyronie’s disease.
key_toxicities: Penile shortening, penile hypo-aesthesia and postoperative erectile dysfunction are reported outcomes of tunical shortening procedures.
monitoring: Measure and document penile length before and after straightening.

therapies_index.name: Modified Nesbit
approved_indications: Tunical shortening for Peyronie’s disease.
key_toxicities: Penile shortening, penile hypoesthesia and de novo erectile dysfunction are reported in studies of this procedure.
monitoring: Measure and document penile length before and after straightening.

therapies_index.name: Yachia
therapies_index.mechanism: A longitudinal tunical incision is closed transversely, shortening the convex side of the penis.
approved_indications: Plication or tunical shortening for penile curvature.
key_toxicities: Penile shortening, penile hypoesthesia and de novo erectile dysfunction are reported in studies of this procedure.
monitoring: Measure and document penile length before and after straightening.

therapies_index.name: Essed-Schröeder
approved_indications: Plication for congenital penile curvature.

therapies_index.name: 16-dot
therapies_index.mechanism: Two pairs of parallel Essed-Schroeder plications are tensioned according to the curvature.
approved_indications: Plication for congenital penile curvature or selected Peyronie’s disease deformities.
key_toxicities: Penile shortening, penile hypoesthesia and de novo erectile dysfunction are reported in studies of this procedure.
monitoring: Measure and document penile length before and after straightening.

therapies_index.name: Simple plication
therapies_index.mechanism: Tunical plications straighten the penis without incising or excising the tunica albuginea.
approved_indications: Tunical shortening for selected patients with Peyronie’s disease.
key_toxicities: Penile shortening, penile hypoesthesia and de novo erectile dysfunction are reported in studies of this procedure.
monitoring: Measure and document penile length before and after straightening.

therapies_index.name: corporal body de-rotation
approved_indications: An approach described for correcting ventral congenital penile curvature.

therapies_index.name: Nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs)
approved_indications: Penile pain during active-phase Peyronie’s disease.
Flu-like symptoms associated with IFN-α2b injections.
therapies_index.administration: For IFN-α2b-associated symptoms, NSAIDs may be given before injection.
monitoring: Periodically reassess pain and treatment efficacy during therapy for Peyronie’s disease.

therapies_index.name: phosphodiesterase type 5 inhibitors
therapies_index.mechanism: Proposed to reduce collagen deposition and increase apoptosis through inhibition of transforming growth factor (TGF)-b1.
approved_indications: Concomitant erectile dysfunction in Peyronie’s disease, or deformity that makes penetrative intercourse difficult, to optimise penetration.

therapies_index.name: tadalafil
approved_indications: Investigated in studies of Peyronie’s disease, including patients with acute-phase disease and erectile dysfunction; the treatment algorithm also lists it as an option when addressing pain in active disease.
therapies_index.administration: A retrospective observational study used Tadalafil 5 mg once daily and assessed curvature progression at 12 weeks.

therapies_index.name: sildenafil
approved_indications: Investigated for erectile function and pain in Peyronie’s disease and as an addition after CCH treatment.
therapies_index.administration: One study used sildenafil 50 mg for twelve weeks; a combined-treatment study used sildenafil 25 mg twice daily after CCH treatment.

therapies_index.name: pentoxifylline
therapies_index.administration: Oral treatment is not recommended for Peyronie’s disease because efficacy has not been proven.

therapies_index.name: vitamin E
therapies_index.administration: Oral treatment is not recommended for Peyronie’s disease because efficacy has not been proven; a comparative study used vitamin E (400 IU) for twelve weeks.

therapies_index.name: tamoxifen
therapies_index.administration: Oral treatment is not recommended for Peyronie’s disease.
key_toxicities: The guideline cites adverse effects as a reason oral tamoxifen is no longer recommended.

therapies_index.name: procarbazine
therapies_index.administration: Listed among oral treatments not recommended for Peyronie’s disease because efficacy has not been proven.

therapies_index.name: potassium para-aminobenzoate (potaba)
therapies_index.administration: Oral treatment is not recommended for Peyronie’s disease because efficacy has not been proven.

therapies_index.name: omega-3 fatty acids
therapies_index.administration: Listed among oral treatments not recommended for Peyronie’s disease because efficacy has not been proven.

therapies_index.name: L-carnitine
therapies_index.administration: Its combination with vitamin E is listed among oral treatments not recommended for Peyronie’s disease because efficacy has not been proven.

therapies_index.name: acetyl esters of carnitine
therapies_index.administration: Oral treatment is not recommended for Peyronie’s disease.

therapies_index.name: colchicine
therapies_index.administration: Oral treatment is not recommended for Peyronie’s disease.

therapies_index.name: verapamil
therapies_index.administration: Intralesional and topical use are discussed for Peyronie’s disease. Evidence is insufficient to support clinical use of injected calcium channel blockers, and evidence of adequate delivery of topical treatment into the tunica albuginea is insufficient.

therapies_index.name: nicardipine
therapies_index.administration: Intralesional use in Peyronie’s disease is discussed, but the evidence is insufficient to support clinical use.

therapies_index.name: Collagenase Clostridium Histolyticum
therapies_index.mechanism: This bacterial enzyme selectively acts on collagen, the main constituent of Peyronie’s disease plaque.
approved_indications: The guideline recommends intralesional treatment for patients with stable Peyronie’s disease, dorsal or lateral curvature > 30 degrees, and a preference for non-surgical care; it notes a substantial placebo effect.

EMA approval described in the guideline concerned non-surgical treatment of stable disease with a palpable dorsal plaque, nonventrally located plaques and curvature of 30-90o. The manufacturer has withdrawn the product from the European market.
therapies_index.administration: The original protocol used two injections of 0.58 mg of CCH 24-72 hours apart every 6 weeks for up to four cycles. A proposed shortened protocol used a single 0.9 mg injection per cycle along three lines around maximal curvature, for up to three cycles at 4-weekly intervals, with home stretching, modelling and VED instead of clinician modelling. Administration should be by a trained, experienced healthcare professional.
key_toxicities: Penile haematoma (50.2%), penile pain (33.5%), penile swelling (28.9%) and injection site pain (24.1%) were reported in treated patients and generally resolved within 14 days.
Serious treatment-emergent adverse events (0.9%) included penile haematoma and corporeal rupture requiring surgery.

therapies_index.name: IFN-α2b
approved_indications: Intralesional treatment of stable-phase Peyronie’s disease; the recommendation specifies stable dorsal or lateral curvature > 30 degrees in patients seeking a minimally invasive option.
therapies_index.administration: Intralesional injections of 5x10^6 units of IFN-α2b in 10 mL saline every 2 weeks over 12 weeks, for a total of six injections.
key_toxicities: Sinusitis and flu-like symptoms.

therapies_index.name: betamethasone
therapies_index.administration: Intralesional administration was examined in a placebo-controlled study; the guideline advises against intralesional steroids to reduce curvature, plaque size or pain.
key_toxicities: Tissue atrophy, thinning of the skin and immunosuppression are reported for intralesional steroids.

therapies_index.name: hyaluronic acid
therapies_index.administration: Intralesional treatment, alone or combined with oral administration, has been studied in Peyronie’s disease. The guideline advises against use to reduce curvature, plaque size or pain outside a clinical trial.

therapies_index.name: botulinum toxin
therapies_index.administration: Intralesional injection has been evaluated in only a single study; evidence is insufficient to support clinical use.

therapies_index.name: Platelet Rich Plasma (PRP)
therapies_index.administration: Intralesional use for Peyronie’s disease is considered experimental and should not be offered outside a clinical trial to reduce curvature, plaque size or pain.

therapies_index.name: H-100 Gel
therapies_index.administration: Applied topically to the penile shaft; evidence is insufficient that adequate amounts reach the tunica albuginea.

therapies_index.name: iontophoresis
therapies_index.administration: Discussed as an adjunct to topical penile treatment; the evidence summary reports no efficacy data.

therapies_index.name: extracorporeal shockwave treatment (ESWT)
approved_indications: May be used for penile pain during acute-phase Peyronie’s disease; it should not be used to improve curvature or reduce plaque size.

therapies_index.name: penile traction therapy (PTT)
therapies_index.mechanism: Proposed disease-modifying mechanisms include collagen remodelling through reduced myofibroblast activity and increased matrix metalloproteinase activity.
approved_indications: Traction devices may be offered to reduce Peyronie’s disease deformity or as part of multimodal treatment, although outcome evidence is limited; evidence does not support a definitive recommendation for monotherapy.
therapies_index.administration: The device may require use for 2-8 hours daily over an extended period.
key_toxicities: Discomfort and inconvenience may occur; the cited studies reported no serious adverse effects.

therapies_index.name: Vacuum Erection Device
therapies_index.mechanism: Application dilates cavernous sinuses, reduces retrograde venous flow and increases arterial inflow.
approved_indications: Vacuum devices may be offered to reduce penile deformity or as part of multimodal Peyronie’s disease treatment, although outcome evidence is limited.

therapies_index.name: injectable verapamil associated with antioxidants and local diclofenac
approved_indications: A long-term study investigated this combination for Peyronie’s disease and reported greater pain reduction than with verapamil alone.
therapies_index.administration: Injectable verapamil was combined with antioxidants and local diclofenac; doses and schedule are not specified.

therapies_index.name: sildenafil 25 mg twice daily after CCH treatment
approved_indications: A study suggested improved curvature and erectile function compared with CCH alone; the findings require external validation.
therapies_index.administration: sildenafil 25 mg twice daily after a shortened CCH protocol combined with VED.

therapies_index.name: tunical shortening procedures
therapies_index.mechanism: Straighten the penis by shortening its longer, convex side.
approved_indications: First surgical option for congenital penile curvature and for Peyronie’s disease with adequate penile length and rigidity, less severe curvature and no hourglass or hinge deformity.
therapies_index.administration: Includes excisional, incisional and plication approaches; no individual approach has proved superior.
key_toxicities: Penile shortening is the most frequently reported adverse outcome; recurrent curvature, penile hypo-aesthesia and postoperative erectile dysfunction are also reported.
monitoring: Measure and document penile length before and after the straightening procedure.

therapies_index.name: tunical lengthening procedures
therapies_index.mechanism: An incision or partial excision on the concave side creates a tunical defect that is covered with a graft to correct curvature or complex deformity while limiting shortening.
approved_indications: Peyronie’s disease with normal erectile function and inadequate penile length, severe curvature or a complex hourglass or hinge deformity.
therapies_index.administration: Grafting may be combined with plication or shortening to address residual curvature; no graft has proved superior.
key_toxicities: Postoperative erectile dysfunction, including a risk of up to 50% in patients without pre-operative erectile dysfunction; penile shortening and numbness may also occur.

therapies_index.name: plaque incision and grafting
therapies_index.mechanism: An incision at the deformity creates a defect covered with graft material.
approved_indications: A tunical lengthening approach for selected Peyronie’s disease deformities; it may also be considered when substantial curvature remains after prosthesis placement and modelling.
key_toxicities: Postoperative erectile dysfunction and penile numbness are potential risks of lengthening surgery.

therapies_index.name: synthetic grafts
therapies_index.administration: The guideline recommends against their use in Peyronie’s disease reconstructive surgery.
key_toxicities: Infection, graft-associated inflammation and fibrosis, graft contraction and possible allergic reactions.

therapies_index.name: Dacron®
therapies_index.administration: Named as a synthetic graft that should be avoided in Peyronie’s disease reconstruction.
key_toxicities: The guideline attributes infection, inflammation and fibrosis, contraction and possible allergic reactions to synthetic grafts.

therapies_index.name: Gore-Tex®
therapies_index.administration: Named as a synthetic graft that should be avoided in Peyronie’s disease reconstruction.
key_toxicities: The guideline attributes infection, inflammation and fibrosis, contraction and possible allergic reactions to synthetic grafts.

therapies_index.name: dermis
approved_indications: Described as an autograft previously used for Peyronie’s disease reconstruction.
key_toxicities: Dermal grafts are associated with veno-occlusive erectile dysfunction (20%) and have not been used in contemporary series.

therapies_index.name: vein grafts
approved_indications: Described as autografts for Peyronie’s disease reconstruction.
therapies_index.administration: The saphenous vein is identified as the vein graft used most often.
key_toxicities: Harvesting complications are possible with autologous grafts.

therapies_index.name: tunica albuginea grafts
approved_indications: Described as autografts for Peyronie’s disease reconstruction.
key_toxicities: Harvestable size is limited; harvesting may weaken penile support and complicate later penile prosthesis implantation.

therapies_index.name: tunica vaginalis
approved_indications: Described as an autograft for Peyronie’s disease reconstruction.
key_toxicities: Harvesting complications are possible with autologous grafts.

therapies_index.name: buccal mucosa
approved_indications: Described as an autograft for Peyronie’s disease reconstruction.
key_toxicities: Harvesting complications are possible with autologous grafts.

therapies_index.name: pericardium
approved_indications: Cadaveric and bovine pericardium are described as graft materials for Peyronie’s disease reconstruction.

therapies_index.name: fascia lata
approved_indications: Autologous and cadaveric fascia lata are described as graft materials for Peyronie’s disease reconstruction.
key_toxicities: Harvesting complications are possible when an autologous graft is used.

therapies_index.name: temporalis fascia
approved_indications: Described as an autologous or cadaveric graft material for Peyronie’s disease reconstruction.
key_toxicities: Harvesting complications are possible when an autologous graft is used.

therapies_index.name: dura mater
therapies_index.administration: Cadaveric dura mater is no longer used as a Peyronie’s disease graft because of infection concerns.
key_toxicities: Possible infection.

therapies_index.name: Porcine SIS
therapies_index.mechanism: This porcine small-intestinal submucosal graft is described as supporting tissue-specific regeneration, angiogenesis and host-cell growth.
approved_indications: Described as a xenograft for Peyronie’s disease reconstruction.

therapies_index.name: bovine dermis
approved_indications: Described as a xenograft for Peyronie’s disease reconstruction.

therapies_index.name: porcine dermis
approved_indications: Described as a xenograft for Peyronie’s disease reconstruction.

therapies_index.name: TachoSil®
therapies_index.mechanism: The collagen fleece also has a haemostatic effect when used as a graft.
approved_indications: Described as a xenograft used in Peyronie’s disease surgery.

therapies_index.name: penile prosthesis implantation
approved_indications: Peyronie’s disease with erectile dysfunction that does not respond to pharmacotherapy; additional straightening may be required.
therapies_index.administration: If residual curvature after implantation is < 30°, no further straightening is indicated. For curvature > 30°, modelling is the first step; persistent deviation > 30° may require further surgery.
key_toxicities: Penile shortening may cause dissatisfaction; additional modelling carries a reported small risk of urethral perforation (3%).

therapies_index.name: inflatable prostheses (IPPs)
approved_indications: Described as a prosthesis option for Peyronie’s disease with erectile dysfunction unresponsive to conventional medical treatment.
therapies_index.administration: The surgeon advises on prosthesis type, while the patient ultimately chooses the implant.
key_toxicities: Patients should be counselled that a prosthesis is not designed to restore their previous penile length.

therapies_index.name: malleable prostheses
approved_indications: Described as a prosthesis option for Peyronie’s disease with erectile dysfunction unresponsive to conventional medical treatment.

therapies_index.name: modelling
therapies_index.mechanism: Bending an inflated penile prosthesis against the direction of curvature aims to straighten residual deformity.
approved_indications: First straightening manoeuvre when intra-operative curvature after penile prosthesis placement is > 30°.
therapies_index.administration: With the prosthesis maximally inflated, it is manually bent opposite the curvature for 90 seconds.
key_toxicities: Urethral perforation (3%) has been reported with modelling over an inflated prosthesis.

therapies_index.name: sliding
therapies_index.administration: Described for simultaneous prosthesis implantation and length restoration in selected end-stage Peyronie’s disease, but the guideline recommends against its use.
key_toxicities: Glans necrosis and other potentially life-changing complications.

therapies_index.name: MoST
approved_indications: Described as an approach for selected patients with end-stage Peyronie’s disease, erectile dysfunction and marked penile shortening.
therapies_index.administration: Should be undertaken only by experienced high-volume surgeons after full patient counselling.

therapies_index.name: MUST
approved_indications: Described as an approach for selected patients with end-stage Peyronie’s disease, erectile dysfunction and marked penile shortening.
therapies_index.administration: Should be undertaken only by experienced high-volume surgeons after full patient counselling.

therapies_index.name: MIT
approved_indications: Described as an approach for selected patients with end-stage Peyronie’s disease, erectile dysfunction and marked penile shortening.
therapies_index.administration: Should be undertaken only by experienced high-volume surgeons after full patient counselling.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Men with low sexual desire in whom psychological or relationship factors contribute.
decision_rules: Tailor treatment to the underlying cause.
Consider sexual thoughts, anxiety, expectations, the role of the partner, and whether diminished desire concerns partnered or solitary sexual activity.
Evidence for psychological interventions is limited, so interpret their potential benefit cautiously.

recommended_regimens.name: Psychological interventions with a focus on cognitive and behavioural strategies
recommended_regimens.summary: These approaches may help men with low sexual desire.

alternative_regimens.name: Mindfulness treatments
alternative_regimens.summary: Presented as a potentially useful psychological approach.

alternative_regimens.name: Couple-focused intervention
alternative_regimens.summary: Address distress related to differences in partners’ sexual desire rather than identifying one partner as the sole patient.
alternative_regimens.conditions_for_use: Consider when the couple experiences distress from discrepant desire, including concurrent age-related changes.

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: The guide describes scarce efficacy data for psychological treatment.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Men whose low sexual desire accompanies signs and symptoms of testosterone deficiency.
treatment_pathways.biomarker_condition: Low testosterone levels associated with low sexual desire.
decision_rules: Offer testosterone therapy when low sexual desire is associated with signs and symptoms of testosterone deficiency.
Aim for a physiological testosterone range.

recommended_regimens.name: testosterone therapy
recommended_regimens.summary: Different testosterone formulations can be used when low testosterone contributes to diminished desire; a cited meta-analysis found favourable effects on sexual motivation and sexual thoughts.

response_assessment.interpretation: The treatment objective is the physiological range.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Men with low sexual desire associated with hyperprolactinaemia caused by a prolactin-secreting pituitary adenoma.
decision_rules: A prolactin-secreting pituitary adenoma is an important possible cause of hyperprolactinaemia-associated low sexual desire; the guide describes pituitary MRI as a means of diagnosis.

recommended_regimens.name: dopamine agonist agents
recommended_regimens.summary: May be used to treat a prolactin-secreting pituitary adenoma associated with low sexual desire.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Men whose low sexual desire accompanies hypothyroidism, hyperthyroidism or diabetes.
decision_rules: Treat the accompanying endocrine disorder according to the disorder involved.
treatment_pathways.special_considerations: The guide does not specify regimens for these endocrine disorders.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Men whose low sexual desire is related to major depression.
decision_rules: Pharmacotherapy may be used for major depression, while taking account of adverse effects on sexual function.
Select antidepressant compounds with less impact on sexual function.
Psychotherapy may increase the effectiveness of pharmacotherapy, particularly when depression accounts for diminished desire.

recommended_regimens.name: Psychotherapy
recommended_regimens.summary: May be combined with depression pharmacotherapy to improve its effectiveness in patients whose low sexual desire is attributable to depression.

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: Antidepressants may impair sexual functioning; no individual antidepressant is specified.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Men receiving chronic treatment that adversely affects sexual desire.
decision_rules: Adjust chronic therapies that negatively affect desire.

recommended_regimens.name: Modulation of chronic therapies
recommended_regimens.summary: Modify ongoing treatment when it has an adverse effect on sexual desire.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Individuals with congenital penile curvature causing significant functional difficulty during intercourse.
decision_rules: Surgery is the definitive treatment and should generally wait until after puberty; it may be performed at any point in adult life when intercourse is substantially impaired.
Although a survey suggested potential advantages of childhood correction, the guide discourages it because penile growth is not yet complete.
No direct comparative studies establish a single superior surgical technique.

recommended_regimens.name: Nesbit procedure
recommended_regimens.summary: Use to correct congenital curvature satisfactorily.

recommended_regimens.name: plication techniques
recommended_regimens.summary: Use with or without medial or lateral neurovascular bundle dissection to correct congenital curvature.

alternative_regimens.name: corporal body de-rotation
alternative_regimens.summary: Described as another approach to ventral curvature, with reported minimal narrowing and shortening.
alternative_regimens.conditions_for_use: No comparative evidence establishes when this approach should be preferred.

not_recommended.name: Surgical correction in childhood
not_recommended.reason: The guide discourages surgery before penile growth has reached its maximum.

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: The guide also describes 16-dot, Yachia and Essed-Schröeder plication techniques, with or without neurovascular bundle elevation and complete penile degloving.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Patients with active or early-stage disease, especially those with penile pain.
decision_rules: Conservative care in early disease primarily seeks to relieve symptoms and limit progression; it may also be used when the patient declines other options during the active phase.
Use pain-directed treatment in the acute phase and reassess pain periodically.
Discuss available treatments and their outcomes before treatment begins.

recommended_regimens.name: nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs
recommended_regimens.summary: Use for penile pain during the acute phase.

alternative_regimens.name: extracorporeal shockwave treatment
alternative_regimens.summary: May be used for acute-phase penile pain, but not to correct curvature or reduce plaque size; the formal recommendation is Weak.

not_recommended.name: extracorporeal shockwave treatment for penile curvature or plaque size
not_recommended.reason: Trials found pain relief but no improvement in curvature or plaque size; the recommendation against these uses is Strong.

response_assessment.method: Reassess penile pain and treatment efficacy.

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: The treatment algorithm also lists tadalafil or LI-ESWT for consideration in active-phase pain control.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Patients with concomitant erectile dysfunction or deformity that makes penetrative intercourse difficult.
decision_rules: Use erectile-function treatment to optimise penetration when erectile dysfunction coexists or deformity impedes intercourse.
Response to erectile dysfunction pharmacotherapy helps determine subsequent surgical choices.

recommended_regimens.name: phosphodiesterase type 5 inhibitors
recommended_regimens.summary: Use for concomitant erectile dysfunction or when deformity impairs penetration.
recommended_regimens.key_outcomes: In a retrospective observational study of acute-phase disease with erectile dysfunction, curvature progression at 12 weeks was 25.9% with Tadalafil 5 mg once daily versus 39.7% in controls (p = 0.042); mean SHIM, PDQ-Overall and PDQPenile Pain scores improved significantly in the treated group (p < 0.001).

response_assessment.method: Assess curvature progression and erectile-function and symptom scores in the context of the cited Tadalafil study.
response_assessment.interpretation: These are observational study results, not an established treatment-response threshold.

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: A separate study reported better pain and IIEF outcomes with sildenafil 50 mg than with vitamin E (400 IU) after twelve weeks; this finding does not override the guide’s recommendation against oral vitamin E for Peyronie’s disease.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Patients unsuitable for surgery or unwilling to undergo it.
decision_rules: Offer conservative management when surgery is unsuitable or unacceptable.
Counsel patients fully about available options and expected outcomes before starting treatment.
Do not offer the listed oral therapies for Peyronie’s disease.

not_recommended.name: vitamin E
not_recommended.reason: Oral treatment lacks convincing evidence of efficacy; the recommendation not to offer it is Strong.

not_recommended.name: potassium para-aminobenzoate (potaba)
not_recommended.reason: Oral treatment lacks convincing evidence of efficacy; the recommendation not to offer it is Strong.

not_recommended.name: tamoxifen
not_recommended.reason: Oral treatment is not recommended; the evidence summary cites adverse effects and the recommendation not to offer it is Strong.

not_recommended.name: pentoxifylline
not_recommended.reason: Oral treatment lacks convincing evidence of efficacy; the recommendation not to offer it is Strong.

not_recommended.name: colchicine
not_recommended.reason: The guide explicitly recommends against offering it orally for Peyronie’s disease.

not_recommended.name: acetyl esters of carnitine
not_recommended.reason: Oral treatment lacks convincing evidence of efficacy; the recommendation not to offer it is Strong.

not_recommended.name: procarbazine
not_recommended.reason: The guide does not recommend this oral treatment because efficacy has not been proven.

not_recommended.name: omega-3 fatty acids
not_recommended.reason: The guide does not recommend this oral treatment because efficacy has not been proven.

not_recommended.name: combination of vitamin E and L-carnitine
not_recommended.reason: The guide does not recommend this oral combination because efficacy has not been proven.

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: The formal recommendations to offer conservative care to this population and to counsel before treatment are both Strong. The guide notes that ineffective oral treatment may delay more effective care.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Patients with stable Peyronie’s disease, a palpable plaque and dorsal or lateral curvature > 30 degrees who seek nonsurgical treatment.
decision_rules: Offer intralesional Collagenase Clostridium Histolyticum for eligible patients requesting nonsurgical care, while explaining the substantial placebo-associated effect and treatment cost.
The approval described in the guide concerned stable disease, palpable dorsal plaques, nonventrally located plaques and curvature of 30-90o.
Administration requires a healthcare professional experienced and trained in this treatment.

recommended_regimens.name: Collagenase Clostridium Histolyticum
recommended_regimens.summary: Intralesional therapy for the specified stable-disease population. CCH has been withdrawn from the European market by its manufacturer, although the guide retains its evidence and recommendation.
recommended_regimens.key_outcomes: The reported average curvature improvement was 34% with treatment versus 18.2% in the placebo group. The IMPRESS studies reported physical and psychological improvement.
recommended_regimens.duration_cycles: Original protocol: two injections of 0.58 mg, 24-72 hours apart, every 6 weeks for up to four cycles.

alternative_regimens.name: modified short protocol
alternative_regimens.summary: A proposed CCH protocol replaces clinician modelling with home stretching, modelling and VED; non-randomised studies reported results comparable to the IMPRESS trials.
alternative_regimens.conditions_for_use: Single injection of 0.9 mg per cycle, placed along three lines near maximal curvature, for up to three cycles separated by 4-weekly intervals.

response_assessment.interpretation: A cited post hoc analysis reported better results with curvature < 60o, onset > 2 years earlier, absence of plaque calcification and good erectile function; these findings do not establish a required response threshold.

supportive_care: Advise against sexual intercourse for the four weeks following injection to reduce the risk of serious treatment-emergent adverse events.
treatment_pathways.special_considerations: Most treated patients experienced at least one mild or moderate local adverse event; reported events included penile haematoma (50.2%), penile pain (33.5%), penile swelling (28.9%) and injection site pain (24.1%), generally resolving within 14 days. Serious treatment-emergent adverse events occurred in 0.9% and included haematoma and corporeal rupture requiring surgery. Preliminary data suggest possible efficacy and safety in active disease, but the formal recommendation specifies stable disease. A proposed role in reducing severe curvature enough to permit plication rather than grafting needs further validation.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Patients with stable dorsal or lateral curvature > 30 degrees who seek a minimally invasive procedure.
decision_rules: Offer intralesional interferon alpha-2b to the specified stable-curvature population.

recommended_regimens.name: interferon alpha-2b
recommended_regimens.summary: Intralesional treatment may improve curvature, plaque characteristics and pain. The guide reports effectiveness regardless of plaque location.
recommended_regimens.key_outcomes: A cited study found significant improvements in curvature, plaque size and density, and pain versus placebo; the guide reports a > 20% reduction in curvature in most treated men, irrespective of plaque location.
recommended_regimens.duration_cycles: 5x10^6 units of IFN-α2b in 10 mL saline every 2 weeks over 12 weeks, for a total of six injections.

response_assessment.method: Assess curvature, plaque size and density, and pain.
response_assessment.interpretation: These outcomes were measured in the cited intralesional-treatment study.

supportive_care: NSAIDs before IFN-α2b injection can treat the reported sinusitis and flu-like symptoms.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Patients considering additional nonsurgical approaches to penile deformity.
decision_rules: Penile traction devices or vacuum devices may be offered to reduce deformity or as components of multimodal treatment, with disclosure that outcome data are limited.
Evidence is insufficient for a definitive recommendation on penile traction therapy as monotherapy.
Do not use the explicitly discouraged intralesional treatments outside the circumstances specified by the guide.

recommended_regimens.name: penile traction devices
recommended_regimens.summary: May be offered for deformity reduction or within multimodal care; evidence for monotherapy and adjunctive use has substantial limitations.
recommended_regimens.key_outcomes: A cited meta-analysis reported an average stretched penile length increase of 1 cm with adjunctive PTT versus no adjunctive PTT, without a significant between-group curvature change. A subset analysis reported a 0.4 cm length increase with device use for > 3 hours/day.
recommended_regimens.duration_cycles: Studies describe device use for 2-8 hours daily.

recommended_regimens.name: vacuum devices
recommended_regimens.summary: May be offered for deformity reduction or as part of multimodal treatment, although evidence is limited.

not_recommended.name: intralesional steroids
not_recommended.reason: Do not offer to reduce curvature, plaque size or pain; a placebo-controlled study found no statistically significant improvement, and reported adverse effects include tissue atrophy, skin thinning and immunosuppression.

not_recommended.name: intralesional platelet-rich plasma
not_recommended.reason: Do not use outside a clinical trial to reduce curvature, plaque size or pain; efficacy remains unproven and the treatment is considered experimental.

not_recommended.name: intralesional hyaluronic acid, alone or combined with oral treatment
not_recommended.reason: The formal Strong recommendation prohibits use for curvature, plaque size or pain outside a clinical trial, despite favourable findings in some cited studies.

not_recommended.name: intralesional botox injections
not_recommended.reason: Evidence from a single study is insufficient to support routine clinical use.

not_recommended.name: topical verapamil and H-100 Gel
not_recommended.reason: Evidence is insufficient that application to the penile shaft achieves adequate active-compound levels in the tunica albuginea.

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: Studies of adjunctive traction with interferon, verapamil or CCH generally did not show significant curvature or length gains, apart from the reported subset result. Data from combined CCH and VED treatment reported mean curvature improvement of -17o and penile length change of +0.4 cm, but lacked a control group that could isolate the VED effect. Evidence for intralesional verapamil and nicardipine is contradictory and insufficient to support clinical use; the guide does not present them as preferred alternatives.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Patients with functionally significant deformity that compromises intercourse and has remained stable for at least three months without pain or worsening deformity.
decision_rules: Operate only after disease stability and when deformity compromises intercourse; the formal recommendation states that stability for at least three months is usually reached after twelve months from symptom onset.
Assess penile length, curvature, erectile function and response to pharmacotherapy if erectile dysfunction is present, complex deformities, and patient expectations before choosing an operation.
Discuss the intended functional result and potential surgical harms before obtaining an informed decision.
Choose among tunical shortening, tunical lengthening and prosthesis implantation according to anatomy and erectile function.
treatment_pathways.special_considerations: The guide also describes stable disease for 3-6 months or surgery more than 9-12 months after onset. Failed conservative treatment, extensive plaques or patient preference may additionally favour surgery once disease is stable. Potential harms discussed include shortening, erectile dysfunction, numbness, delayed orgasm, recurrent or residual curvature, palpable sutures, possible circumcision and further wasting after shortening procedures. Comparative surgical evidence is limited.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Patients with stable disease, adequate penile length and erectile rigidity, less severe curvature, and no hourglass or hinge deformity.
decision_rules: Use a tunical shortening operation as the first surgical option for this anatomy and erectile-function profile.
Select the technique according to surgeon and patient preference; no approach has been proven superior.
Document penile length before and after straightening.

recommended_regimens.name: tunical shortening procedures
recommended_regimens.summary: Correct curvature by shortening the longer, convex side. Described techniques include Nesbit, Yachia, 16-dot and simple plication.
recommended_regimens.key_outcomes: Across the procedures described, complete straightening is reported in > 85% of patients. Penile shortening of 1-1.5 cm was reported in 22-69% of patients; recurrence and penile hypo-aesthesia were uncommon (~10%).

response_assessment.timepoint: Before and after the straightening procedure
response_assessment.interpretation: Length loss is the most commonly reported adverse outcome of shortening procedures.

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: The guide cautions that published outcomes largely come from retrospective studies without adequate comparisons between techniques.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Patients with stable disease and normal erectile function who have inadequate penile length, severe curvature or a complex hourglass or hinge deformity.
decision_rules: Use tunical lengthening for this anatomical profile when erectile function is preserved.
The proposed severe-curvature threshold is > 60o, but the guide states that studies have not validated it.
Choose graft material with the patient; no graft has been proven superior.
Explain that lengthening is intended chiefly to limit shortening and correct complex deformity, not necessarily to provide lasting length gain.

recommended_regimens.name: tunical lengthening procedures
recommended_regimens.summary: Incise or partially excise plaque on the concave side and cover the tunical defect with a graft; additional plication or shortening may be needed for residual curvature.
recommended_regimens.key_outcomes: The guide reports a postoperative erectile dysfunction risk of up to 50% for patients without pre-operative erectile dysfunction.

not_recommended.name: synthetic grafts
not_recommended.reason: A Strong recommendation prohibits their use in reconstructive surgery; reported concerns include infection, inflammatory fibrosis, contracture and possible allergic reactions.

not_recommended.name: cadaveric dura mater
not_recommended.reason: The guide states that it is no longer used because of infection concerns.

supportive_care: Postoperative rehabilitation with VED or PTT has been suggested to limit penile length loss of up to 1.5 cm.
The guide describes daily nocturnal PDE5I to support erections and graft perfusion and potentially reduce postoperative erectile dysfunction.
Penile massage and stretching have been recommended after wound healing.
treatment_pathways.special_considerations: Autografts, allografts and xenografts are described, but the guide does not identify a preferred material. Complete plaque removal may increase postoperative erectile dysfunction through venous leak; partial excision may be permissible with extensive calcification. For repair, the guide recommends non-absorbable or slowly re-absorbed sutures and burying non-absorbable knots to limit skin irritation.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Patients with concomitant erectile dysfunction that does not respond to pharmacotherapy or conventional medical treatment.
decision_rules: Use penile prosthesis implantation, with additional straightening when required.
After implantation, the guide states that residual curvature < 30° needs no further straightening.
For curvature > 30°, first perform modelling with the prosthesis maximally inflated.
If deviation > 30° remains after modelling, consider incision with or without defect coverage, or plaque incision and grafting.

recommended_regimens.name: penile prosthesis implantation
recommended_regimens.summary: Implant a prosthesis for Peyronie’s disease with erectile dysfunction unresponsive to pharmacotherapy; modelling, plication, incision or excision with or without grafting may be added to straighten the penis.

not_recommended.name: sliding technique
not_recommended.reason: A Strong recommendation prohibits its use because of the significant risk of life-changing complications, including reported glans necrosis.

response_assessment.interpretation: At < 30°, no additional straightening is indicated; at > 30°, modelling is the first step.
Deviation > 30° prompts consideration of further straightening.

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: Modelling is described as bending the maximally inflated prosthesis opposite the curvature for 90 seconds; a small risk of urethral perforation (3%) has been reported. The guide describes possible correction of curvature < 30° by the prosthesis itself over the subsequent 6-9 months. Counsel patients that prostheses are not designed to restore previous penile length. MoST, MUST and MIT are described for selected end-stage cases with marked shortening, but only for experienced high-volume surgeons after full counselling.

recommendations.statement: Diagnose and classify low sexual desire (LSD) using medical and sexual history, potentially supplemented by validated questionnaires.
recommendations.source_heading: 7.5 Recommendations for the treatment of low sexual desire

recommendations.statement: Include a physical examination in the initial evaluation of LSD to detect anatomical abnormalities associated with LSD or other sexual dysfunctions, particularly erectile dysfunction.
recommendations.source_heading: 7.5 Recommendations for the treatment of low sexual desire

recommendations.statement: Use laboratory testing to exclude endocrine disorders.
recommendations.context: Initial assessment of low sexual desire.
recommendations.source_heading: 7.5 Recommendations for the treatment of low sexual desire

recommendations.statement: Adjust ongoing treatments that may adversely affect sexual desire.
recommendations.source_heading: 7.5 Recommendations for the treatment of low sexual desire

recommendations.statement: Provide testosterone therapy when LSD occurs with signs and symptoms of testosterone deficiency.
recommendations.source_heading: 7.5 Recommendations for the treatment of low sexual desire

recommendations.statement: Use the Nesbit procedure or a plication technique, with or without medial or lateral neurovascular bundle dissection, to correct the curvature satisfactorily.
recommendations.context: Surgical treatment of congenital penile curvature.
recommendations.source_heading: 8.1.4 Summary of evidence and recommendation for diagnosis and treatment of congenital penile curvature

recommendations.statement: Obtain a medical and sexual history in patients with Peyronie’s disease (PD), covering disease duration, pain during erection, penile deformity, deformity-related difficulty with vaginal or anal intromission, and erectile dysfunction (ED).
recommendations.source_heading: 8.2.2.1 Summary of evidence and recommendations for diagnosis of Peyronie’s disease

recommendations.statement: Examine patients with PD for palpable plaques, stretched or erect penile length, degree of curvature assessed by self-photography, a vacuum-assisted erection test or a pharmacologically induced erection, and related conditions such as Dupuytren’s contracture or Ledderhose disease.
recommendations.source_heading: 8.2.2.1 Summary of evidence and recommendations for diagnosis of Peyronie’s disease

recommendations.statement: Use intracavernous injection during the diagnostic evaluation of PD to assess penile curvature objectively during erection.
recommendations.source_heading: 8.2.2.1 Summary of evidence and recommendations for diagnosis of Peyronie’s disease

recommendations.statement: Use the PD-specific questionnaire, particularly in clinical trials; its routine use in everyday clinical practice is not required.
recommendations.source_heading: 8.2.2.1 Summary of evidence and recommendations for diagnosis of Peyronie’s disease

recommendations.statement: Do not routinely use ultrasound (US), computed tomography or magnetic resonance imaging to evaluate plaque size or penile deformity.
recommendations.source_heading: 8.2.2.1 Summary of evidence and recommendations for diagnosis of Peyronie’s disease
